analysis.investment_thesis: Swasth Foodtech is a 2021-incorporated micro-cap with a trivial 0.17% ROE and no meaningful earnings track record — it fails virtually every quantitative filter I require. At an INR 8.88 Cr market cap in a commoditized refined oils business, there is no margin of safety and no proven earning power to value.
key_strengths: High promoter holding at 72.89% signals skin in the game
Operates in a staple FMCG sub-segment (edible oils) with steady end-demand
Small equity base leaves theoretical room for future growth
key_risks: ROE of 0.17% indicates effectively no earning power on capital deployed
Only ~4 years since incorporation — fails the 5-year positive earnings test
Refined oils is a brutally commoditized, low-margin, import-price-driven business
red_flags: No multi-year earnings history — textbook speculative issue
Negligible profitability (0.17% ROE) inconsistent with going-concern value
Micro-cap BSE SME-type listing with thin liquidity and disclosure
Recent listing/IPO — seller (promoter/banker) knows more than the buyer
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham standpoint, this security does not meet the threshold of an "investment operation." Incorporated in 2021, Swasth Foodtech lacks the 5–10 year earnings record on which intrinsic value must be grounded. A reported ROE of 0.17% is indistinguishable from zero — the business is not earning its cost of capital, let alone producing the stable, demonstrable earning power required to apply a Graham multiplier. Without EPS, book value, current ratio, debt/equity, or interest coverage disclosed here, one cannot even compute the Graham Number; the absence of such data is itself disqualifying for a defensive investor.

The qualitative picture reinforces the quantitative one: refined edible oils is a fiercely commoditized industry where pricing power belongs to large integrated players (Adani Wilmar, Ruchi, Marico, Patanjali) and margins are whipsawed by palm/soy import parity. A four-year-old INR 8.88 Cr micro-cap has neither scale, brand moat, nor distribution edge. High 72.89% promoter holding is a minor positive, but in a recently listed micro-cap it more often signals a thinly floated, promoter-controlled vehicle than shareholder alignment. This is speculation, not investment — Mr. Market may offer it at any price, but it is not for the intelligent investor.
